headline: Approved amended vacant building ordinance, reduced Law Department supplemental appropriation, and Tufts-related resolutions; tabled $571,550 capital fund request.
summary: The council approved changes to the vacant building ordinance and reduced the Law Department supplemental appropriation. It passed resolutions on Tufts University and its workers and referred a noise ordinance update to committee. It tabled a request for $571,550 from the capital stabilization fund.
decisions: Approved 7-0 the resolution in remembrance of John Westwater (26-135).
Approved and referred 7-0 the resolution to update the noise ordinance (26-138) to the Resident Services Committee.
Approved 7-0 the notice of relocation of the Ward 4, Precinct 2 polling place (26-143).
Approved 7-0 the Medford call for the September 1, 2026 state primary election (26-144).
Approved 7-0 the election warrant for the September 1, 2026 state primary (26-145).
Referred the resolution to schedule neighborhood ward meetings (26-024) back to committee, 7-0.
Approved 7-0 the resolution calling on Tufts to re-enroll a graduate worker and provide compensation and support (26-136).
Approved 7-0 the resolution calling on Tufts University to support contract demands of its facilities workers (26-137).
Motion to table the capital and general stabilization fund appropriation requests (26-133) failed, 3-4.
Tabled 5-2 the capital and general stabilization fund appropriation requests (26-133).
Approved 7-0 the board and commission appointments, including Chris D'Aveta to the Zoning Board of Appeals (26-139).
Approved 7-0 the Community Preservation Committee appropriation requests for Playstead Park and Osgood House (26-140).
Approved 7-0 the $1,500.00 payment of an unpaid bill from prior fiscal years to Citizenserve (26-141).
Approved 7-0 an amendment to cut 382,586.70 from the fiscal year 2027 supplemental appropriation and approve 42,507.63 in one-month funding (26-142).
Approved unanimously the council response requesting litigation reports and expenditure categorizations from the City Administration (26-142B).
Approved 4-3 a motion to sever changes 4, 6 and 7 from the amendments to the vacant building ordinance (25-054).
Adopted 4-3 changes 4, 6 and 7 to the vacant building ordinance (25-054).
Approved 7-0 the vacant building ordinance as amended, to be ordained (25-054).
Approved 7-0 the personnel ordinance amendments for the Director and Assistant Director of Health and Human Services (26-124).
Approved 7-0 the resolution to update the ordinance establishing the Medford Commission for Persons with Disabilities (26-063).

237 
 
 
 
 
 
Medford City Council 
Medford, Massachusetts 
 
The Fourteenth Regular Meeting August 4th, 2026 
 
This meeting took place in the City Council Chamber, 2nd Floor, Medford City Hall, 85 George P. Hassett 
Drive, Medford, MA and via Zoom. To submit written comments, please email REliseo@medford-ma.gov. 
 
CALL TO ORDER 
 
President Zac Bears called the Fourteenth Regular Meeting of the Medford City Council to order in the 
Council Chambers and via Zoom. 
 
ROLL CALL 
 
Present: President Bears; Vice President Lazzaro; Councilor Callahan; Councilor Leming; Councilor 
Mullane; Councilor Scarpelli; Councilor Tseng. Seven members were present and no members were 
absent. Inside the Rail: Acting City Clerk Richard Eliseo Jr. 
 
SALUTE TO THE FLAG 
 
 
ANNOUNCEMENTS, ACCOLADES, REMEMBRANCES, REPORTS, AND RECORDS 
 
26-135 - Resolution in Remembrance of John Westwater 
 
 
Whereas, John Westwater lived on Usher Road, steps from the West Medford train station. 
He taught middle school at St. Joseph’s in Medford for many years, where his affectionate 
nickname was “Mister Sister.” His favorite hobbies were camping and going for walks. He 
loved nature, his home, and his neighborhood; and,  
 
Whereas, on July 20th an Amtrak train was passing through the West Medford train station, 
just down the street from where John lived. He was crossing the tracks and was hit. John 
died from his injuries. He was 77 years old; now, therefore: 
 
Be It Resolved by the Medford City Council that we share our deepest condolences with 
Mr. Westwater’s family and loved ones and express our hope that this senseless tragedy 
will not be in vain and will not be repeated.  
 
Be it Further Resolved that we will work with the Massachusetts Bay Transit Authority and 
Amtrak, a quasi-governmental corporation created by Congress in 1970 to preserve 
intercity passenger rail service, to make sorely needed safety improvements to the West 
Medford commuter and Amtrak train station so this will never happen again. 
 
Vice President Lazzaro Motioned to approve (seconded by Councilor Tseng) – 
Approved on a Roll call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed

26-138 - Resolution to Update the Noise Ordinance (to be referred to Resident Services 
Committee) 
 
Whereas, the City of Medford’s Noise Ordinance was last updated in 1974, and is lacking 
any recent updates to types of noise that can impact residents; and  
 
Whereas, residents of Medford have shared a variety of ways in which different noise levels 
have been impacting their daily lives; and  
 
Whereas, noise levels can also be considered a health hazard, and it is left to the 
community to help regulate and advise on noise restrictions throughout their city and 
towns; and  
 
Whereas, the American Public Health Association has stated that “loud noise causes 
hearing loss and tinnitus and can contribute to non-auditory health problems. Chronic 
noise, even at low levels, can cause annoyance, sleep disruption, and stress that 
contribute to cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, metabolic disturbances, 
exacerbation of psychological disorders, and premature mortality. Noise interferes with 
cognition and learning, contributes to behavior problems, and reduces achievement and 
productivity. The health of more than 100 million Americans is at risk, with children among 
the most vulnerable.”; and  
 
Whereas, “The APHA policy statements below relate to this update by advocating for the 
following: reducing environmental stressors and their harmful effects on public health, 
rectifying the disproportionate burden of environmental hazards borne by disadvantaged 
populations, and encouraging actions to mitigate adverse effects. Including noise as a 
stressor in future APHA policy statements and updates is recommended.”  
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that the Council's Resident Services and Public 
Engagement Committee review the current noise ordinance to update its language, 
function, type and current usage. 
 
 
Councilor Mullane motioned to approve and refer 26-138 out to committee (seconded 
by Councilor Tseng) – Approved on a Roll call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed

26-024 - Resolution to Schedule Neighborhood Ward Meetings Hosted by City Council 
 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that the Council's Resident Services and Public 
Engagement Committee discuss a plan to schedule Neighborhood Ward Meetings hosted 
by the City Council in 2026 and 2027.

26-136 - Resolution to Demand Tufts Reinstate Graduate Worker Facing Retaliation and 
Retribution 
 
Whereas, a Tufts University international graduate worker recently faced retaliation by her 
adviser for reporting that they required her to work a significant amount of hours as an 
unpaid teaching assistant, which violated her union contract. Later, the graduate worker 
was removed from her doctoral program; and,  
 
Whereas, the worker and her union identified that there were multiple contract violations 
over the course of the year and the worker has experienced retaliation for protected union 
activity about her working conditions; and,  
 
Whereas, after experiencing this retaliation, Tufts University informed the worker on June 
24th that she was disenrolled from her doctoral program and transferred to the masters of 
science program, forcing her out of the university in August; and,  
 
Whereas, after being forced out of the doctoral program that she intended to complete, her 
student visa is expected to expire in September 2026. This worker was not even given the 
opportunity to find a different adviser at Tufts, and she is not being given sufficient time to 
apply to other doctoral programs or conduct a proper job search; now, therefore:  
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we call on Tufts to immediately re-enroll 
this student in her doctoral program.
243 
 
Be it Further Resolved that we call on Tufts to award this worker compensation for losing 
her summer stipend and losing her doctoral program enrollment after reporting bargaining 
contract violations, provide transitional support to move to a new lab to remain in the 
program, and cease any future tolerance of retribution for protected union activity – 
especially at a university that claims to be committed to advancing equity and justice. 
 
 
Addressing the Council: 
Genesis Perez 229 Main St 
Simon Alcindor 44 Tainter St 
Miccah Kessleman 499 Main St 
 
 
 
 
President Bears motioned to Approve (seconded by Councilor Tseng) – Approved on a 
Roll call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed 
 
 
 
 
26-137 - Resolution to Support Tufts Facilities Workers Bargaining for a Fair Contract 
 
Whereas, the City of Medford and its residents share a strong interest in seeing through a 
good quality union contract between Tufts and its facilities workers who belong to SEIU 
32BJ; and,  
 
Whereas, these essential workers are employed as utility workers, as maintenance 
mechanics, in the grounds department, and in a variety of trades positions such 
carpenters, locksmiths, HVAC mechanics, plumbers, electricians, and more; and,  
 
Whereas, as the largest private employer in Medford and Somerville, and a major Boston-
area employer, Tufts University has a vitally important role in setting standards for all 
working people, particularly those to whom the University owes its buildings’ conditioned 
functioning and its outstanding grounds; and,  
 
Whereas, these proud 32BJ SEIU members’ demands for a fair contract are reasonable: 
fair, family- sustaining wage increases, lower healthcare monthly healthcare premiums, 
protections for immigrant workers, union benefits and other richly deserved 
improvements; now, therefore:  
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we call on Tufts University to support the 
contract demands of Tufts facilities workers and to set an example of fair treatment and 
good labor relations for other area employers. 
 
 
Addressing the Council: 
Patrick Keith 64 Magoon Av 
Simon Alcindor 44 Tainter St 
Ilene Learner 3920 Mystic Valley Pkwy 
Triana  
Miccah Kessleman 499 Main St 
 
 
 
President Bears motioned to Approve (seconded by Councilor Mullane) – Approved on 
a Roll call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed

26-142 - Supplemental Appropriation for the Fiscal Year 2027   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Councilor Tseng motioned to Amend the Appropriation paper to cut 382,586.70 from the 
Appropriation and approve 42,507.63 one-month funding (seconded by Councilor 
Scarpelli) – Approved on a Roll call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed 
 
 
26-142B - Council Response to Paper 26-142 
 
Offered by President Bears 
Motion to Approve: Councilor Tseng 
Approved Unanimously 
 
Whereas, the Medford City Council unanimously approved Resolution 26-043 on February 
24, 2026 requesting a comprehensive litigation report from the City Administration 
regarding the significant increase in legal claims against the City of Medford since January
248 
 
2020 and the financial cost of the City Administration’s decisions regarding litigation 
strategy and employee relations to the city and its residents; and, 
 
Whereas, the Medford City Council unanimously approved Resolution 26-077 on April 28, 
2026 to file a Public Records Request pursuant to state law due to the City 
Administration’s lack of response to the prior request; and, 
 
Whereas, the Medford City Council took numerous votes and councilors provided clarity 
and guidance to the City Administration at dozens of public City Council meetings since 
February 2026 regarding the information requested in the above resolutions; and, 
 
Whereas, the Medford City Council has only received partial and significantly delayed 
responses from the City Administration, including information never requested by the 
Council; and, 
 
Whereas, the Medford City Council was forced to reduce the FY27 Law Department budget 
due to lack of information about past legal expenses and planned FY27 legal expenses in 
order to exercise basic oversight and transparency regarding the FY27 City Budget; and, 
 
Whereas, the City Administration has made repeated statements that they are not capable 
of meeting these requests even after repeated clarifications by the Council; and,  
 
Whereas, the Medford City Council received a document today, August 4, 2026, 
summarizing KP Law expenditures since January 2020 with a total sum of $2.4 million; and,  
 
Whereas, the Chief of Staff informed the City Council by email that she is not able to 
attend tonight’s meeting due to a prior commitment and requested that the Council refer 
any additional questions to the Mayor and Chief of Staff; now, therefore: 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we request the following from the City 
Administration: 
 
1. A written response to Resolution 26-043 with the status of each requested item in 
the Comprehensive Litigation Report and Quarterly Litigation Status Report, 
including an explanation of what efforts have been made to respond to each 
request and why the City Administration cannot provide the requested information, 
if necessary. This explanation may also include any efforts made to respond to the 
Public Records Request authorized by the Council in Resolution 26-077. 
2. A written response to Resolution 26-043’s request for an independent review of the 
City’s litigation costs, practices, and risk management procedures. 
3. A categorization of the August 4, 2026 list of KP Law expenditures into the following 
categories: 
i. Collective bargaining negotiation expenses 
ii. Employee litigation, arbitration, grievance, or other settlement-
related expenses 
iii. Legal review of ordinances or board and commission proceedings 
iv. Non-employee claims and litigation (e.g. vehicle or sewer claims) 
v. Provision of legal guidance to city staff regarding administrative 
actions 
vi. Other legal work 
4. A similar report and categorization of expenditures for any other outside legal 
services provided by firms other than KP Law since 2020. 
5. A financial summary of all settlements or judgments against the city for claims over 
$10,000 since 2020, including the amount paid by the city for each claim and the 
source of funds used to make payment.
249 
 
6. A list and total estimated cost of all budgeted legal expenses for the FY27 city 
budget in department budgets other than the Law Department. 
7. An update on the hiring of a City Solicitor and when the job will be posted. 
 
Be it Further Resolved that the Medford City Council hopes that this further written 
clarification of its numerous and repeated requests for information since February 2026 
will provide the City Administration with appropriate guidance to meet these requests and 
provide a transparent and full accounting of the city’s legal expenses since 2020 to the 
residents of Medford. 
 
Be it Further Resolved that this resolution be submitted to the City Administration 
immediately and the text be placed on the September 15, 2026 City Council Regular 
Meeting Agenda as Paper 26-142B along with any written responses received from the City 
Administration by September 10. 
 
 
Addressing the Council: 
Nick Gurleo  
Andrew Castignetti 
Simon Alcindor 
Miccah Kessleman
